title: Fruit and vegetable smoothie, non-dairy, added protein

content.title: About
content.content: A non-dairy fruit and vegetable smoothie with added protein is a ready‑to‑drink blend of fresh fruits, vegetables and plant‑based protein. It contains no dairy ingredients, making it suitable for vegans and people with lactose intolerance, while providing an extra source of protein for muscle recovery.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Typical blends include spinach, kiwi, mango and berries, delivering a high load of vitamins and antioxidants.
The plant protein is usually derived from pea, hemp or soy isolates.
Non‑dairy smoothies are travel‑friendly: they stay fresh in the fridge for up to 24 hours without flavor loss.
Combining fruits and vegetables boosts dietary fiber intake, supporting digestion.
Some brands fortify the drink with probiotics to aid gut microbiome health.

items.title: Rich in vitamins C and K
items.content: Fruits and leafy greens supply vitamin C for immune support and vitamin K for proper blood clotting.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Added protein provides 10–15 g of protein per serving, helping muscle repair after exercise.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from the fruit‑vegetable mix promotes intestinal motility and a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low added sugar
items.content: The beverage is typically sweetened only with natural fruit sugars, without refined sugar.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Berries and green leaves contain polyphenols that help neutralize free radicals.

items.title: Allergy to plant protein
items.content: Some individuals may react to pea, soy or hemp protein.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Spinach and certain berries are high in oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stones in susceptible people.

items.title: High acidity
items.content: Citrus fruits may increase heartburn in those with a sensitive stomach.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Some ready‑to‑drink smoothies contain added sodium for flavor; people with hypertension should check the label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink the smoothie straight from the bottle, optionally add ice or dilute with water/plant milk. It works well as a post‑workout drink, breakfast replacement, or light snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the smoothie refrigerated at 2–4 °C and consume within 24 hours after opening. After that, taste and aroma may deteriorate.
